gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Nebula Mars 3 reaches its 1,000-lumen rating only on wall power: Soundcore's own battery table rates it at 700 lumens for 1 h 30 min on battery in Standard mode and 300 lumens in Eco mode for 5 h, and an optional brightness setting can switch it to Eco when the adapter is unplugged, so on battery alone it can't play a typical feature film at full brightness.
standout_why: Wirecutter (cited) is the only rival I could read that covers this. It measured about 2 hours of battery at full brightness and 4 h 45 min in an eco mode it describes as 20% brightness, and over 800 lumens on AC. It does not give Soundcore's own battery-mode lumen ratings (700 Standard, 300 Eco) or mention the setting that drops to Eco when unplugged. ChatGPT's card repeats '1,000 ANSI lumens · built-in battery' as if those two go together. None of the pages I read gives the AC-only picks' power draw, which a shopper needs to size a power station. The RTINGS outdoor, portable and X1 pages returned only navigation text, Yahoo and Forbes returned 403, and What Hi-Fi returned only its title, so I couldn't check those pages' text. That is why this is a 2, not a 3.
decides: This confirms the Mars 3 as the only real pick without an outlet, but only for short films or if the shopper accepts 300 lumens, which suits a screen of roughly 80–100 in. after full dark. For a 120–150 in. screen at full brightness, the shopper needs wall power or a power station either way. The X1 measured about 160 W at maximum brightness (about 0.3 kWh for a 2-hour film, per Notebookcheck), and the Horizon 20 is rated at no more than 180 W. A power station of 500 Wh or more covers one movie night with either, so the AC picks plus a power station beat the Mars 3 on battery for big, bright backyard screens.

findings.label: Battery-mode brightness and runtime, Standard mode
findings.note: Soundcore's own per-model table, row 'Mars 3 (D2333)'. The headline rating of 1,000 ANSI lumens therefore applies on AC power only. The page also says 'Standard Mode, while brighter, will shorten the battery life.'

findings.label: Battery-mode brightness and runtime, Eco mode
findings.note: Defined as 'the highest brightness possible while achieving the target battery life specification.' The product page FAQ agrees: 'the display brightness is lowered to 300 lumens to extend the playtime.'

findings.label: Auto switch to Eco when unplugged
findings.value: Optional setting: with it on, unplugging the adapter switches the projector from standard to eco brightness
findings.note: Setting path: Settings > Display & Sound > Picture > Brightness. The page does not name which models have it, and its 'below 20% battery' rule is stated only for the Capsule 3 Laser and Mars 3 Air.

findings.label: Battery capacity
findings.source_title: soundcore Nebula Mars 3 | Outdoor Projector with 5H Long Playtime
findings.note: From the feature bullet. The spec table lists 'Battery Life (Eco Mode) 5 Hrs', 'Power 19V/9.47A' (about 180 W adapter, my arithmetic: 19 × 9.47), 'Brightness 1000 ANSI Lumens' and IPX3. 185 Wh over 1.5 h in Standard mode implies roughly 120 W average draw (my arithmetic).

findings.label: Wirecutter measured battery runtime
findings.value: About 2 h at full brightness; 4 h 45 min in eco mode (20% brightness)
findings.source_title: The 7 Best Projectors of 2026 | Reviews by Wirecutter
findings.note: Wirecutter also measured 'over 800 lumens of maximum brightness' on a 100-inch screen, without saying whether that was on AC or battery. This page is the cited rival, and it already has the runtime half of the finding.

findings.label: Measured power draw at highest brightness
findings.source_title: Notebookcheck: Impressive 4K laser projector with optional 4.1.2 sound – Anker Nebula X1 in a practical test
findings.note: Notebookcheck writes '160 Wh at the highest brightness level', which is a power figure given in energy units. Its own '0.3 kWh for a two-hour movie' is consistent with about 160 W. It concludes 'a compact power station with 500 Wh is therefore sufficient for most movie nights outdoors' and notes the X1 'is always dependent on an external power source.'

findings.label: Built-in battery
findings.source_title: Anker Nebula X1 Smart 4K Portable Projector Review | ProjectorCentral
findings.note: Quote: 'It doesn't have a built-in battery, so you'd need to stick close to power anyway.' ProjectorCentral measured 2,101–2,588 lumens in picture modes and 3,187 in Conference mode (SDR, 100% brightness).

findings.label: Power dissipation / input
findings.value: ≤180 W; AC 100–240 V, 50/60 Hz; no battery
findings.note: Spec rows 'Power Dissipation ≤180W' and 'Battery Capacity /'. Operating temperature 32–104 °F. Price shown: $1,559.00, marked down from $1,699.00. On a 500 Wh station, 500 ÷ 180 ≈ 2.8 h before inverter losses (my arithmetic).
